title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded under the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model version gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces needed to compute that aggregation were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, clarify execution semantics, analyze representative failure modes from archived validator traces, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A practical safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are fed back to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that inserting deterministic verifiers can increase verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and incurring interaction costs [1]–[4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps warn that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor CLI templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. Verifier-guided repair can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics; to guarantee activation we used deterministic controlled faults and a paired design that reuses the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair pipelines have been studied across code, IaC, and DSL domains. Controlled evaluations demonstrate that deterministic verifiers interposed between stochastic generation and acceptance tend to raise verifier-detected pass rates and that feeding verifier diagnostics into a repair model increases the probability a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899; https://openalex.org/W7171267824]. Complementary analyses document caveats: optimization toward a single verifier proxy can produce verifier-exploitation pathologies [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10187492/v1], and verifier-mediated workflows impose a measurable interaction/compute overhead—the so-called "verifier tax"—that depends on horizon and design choices [http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19328]. Survey and field evidence for NetOps indicate LLMs help with read-oriented tasks but provide weaker guarantees for safe closed-loop configuration changes without conservative verification and orchestration [https://openalex.org/W7161165783].

Synthesis and gap. Prior work motivates controlled experiments that (a) use deterministic verifiers, (b) ensure intervention activation, and (c) instrument both correctness outcomes and safety failure modes. The supplied literature supports improvements in verifier pass rates in related domains but leaves open cross-domain generality for vendor CLIs and the net safety effect (harmful over-repair). This study addresses that gap with a preregistered paired, controlled-fault design on vendor-CLI templates.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered under vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the paired difference in the binary indicator that both a deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance check accept the post-repair configuration.

Adapter, pairing, and execution semantics. Confirmatory execution used the adapter family hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under those semantics each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; both arms therefore received the same initial candidate. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of verifier diagnostics) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the repair model. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Because the adapter contract provided a single shared initial generation per pair, this design isolates the effect of diagnostics exposure under a matched repair budget and matched source generation; it does not measure effects of independent first-pass sampling across conditions.

Controlled-challenge task bank and scoring. A deterministic controlled-fault generator produced 40 preregistered task indices with realistic actionable violations (examples: dropped required restore, protected-interface change, make-before-break uplink switchover). The primary success predicate required agreement of two deterministic checks: the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check that together decide valid/invalid for the episode. A frozen harmful-change labeling mapping (used for the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation) marked an episode as harmful if post-repair validator traces included PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; that mapping and the per-episode validator traces were recorded during execution and enable deterministic recomputation of the preregistered safety statistic.

Execution and exclusion rules. The preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule excludes a pair only if both executions are unscorable for infrastructure reasons. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; confirmatory execution produced 39 complete pairs because one source generation was invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule. Model-call budget for confirmatory execution was 120; the run consumed 118 hosted-model calls.

Statistical analysis plan. The predefined primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent exact paired binomial). We report discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the paired absolute risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Sensitivity analyses for missingness (treated-as-failure) were preregistered; all per-episode traces and scored artifacts required to recompute aggregations were recorded.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes correspond to 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded under preregistered rule). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcome (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Missingness and preregistered safety aggregation. The preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule excluded one pair because its source generation was invalid/unscorable. The archived confirmatory analysis produced the primary paired binary result but did not include the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation in its confirmatory summary; therefore we do not present a confirmatory safety verdict here. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validator traces required to compute that preregistered statistic were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation by auditors; any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary are exploratory.
sections.discussion:
Primary interpretation. The confirmatory paired result shows a substantial and statistically detectable increase in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic verifier diagnostics are exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.0215). The paired design isolates diagnostics exposure because both arms received the same initial controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets; therefore observed differences are attributable to the information-treatment (exposed diagnostics) rather than differing initial candidates or additional repair calls.

Discordant-pair structure and mechanism. The discordant-pair pattern (n10 = 9 guarded-only; n01 = 1 baseline-only) indicates most improvements came from repairs that, when provided validator diagnostics, avoided residual violations that blind repair failed to fix. Representative archived episodes illustrate the mechanism: task-000003 (difficulty level = hard; see artifact_examples) shows baseline produced a post-repair trace with PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE violations (validation_after.violation_codes present) and score = 0, while the guarded execution for the same shared controlled-fault candidate produced a corrected sequence accepted by the verifier+simulator (score = 1). In other representative episodes (e.g., task-000001) the source candidate initially violated FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH; guarded repair consumed explicit violation codes and produced an edit ordering that restored required command sequences and satisfied both checks. These per-episode validator_trace fields (violation_codes, injected_validation.difficulty, validation_after) recorded in execution artifacts directly support the case that exposed diagnostics enable more targeted corrective edits rather than simply producing more diverse restarts.

Difficulty-stratified and workflow-pattern interpretation. The archived task manifest and representative artifacts show a range of difficulty patterns (labeled medium, hard, very_hard) and workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break, paired MTU atomic change, shutdown–configure–restore). The guarded condition achieved near-ceiling success (97.44%) across this preregistered controlled bank; because guarded is close to 100% on this task set, remaining room for improvement is constrained and effect-size interpretation must account for ceiling effects. The observed improvement despite heterogenous difficulty patterns suggests diagnostics exposure helps across multiple workflow patterns, but the present sample size and task scope limit claims about systematic heterogeneity by fault class (per-fault-class analyses are exploratory and require independent confirmatory replication).

Statistical uncertainty and preregistered planning. The preregistration planned detectable effects near ~30 percentage points with n=40; the observed absolute paired difference (20.51%) is smaller than that planning target but achieved statistical significance under the exact paired test given the observed discordant counts. The 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI ([0.0769, 0.3590]) quantifies remaining uncertainty and indicates the effect is unlikely to be trivial in this controlled bank but could be smaller or larger in other settings.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Exposing diagnostics materially improved verifier-defined correctness on the tested controlled fault bank, but verifier-guided workflows require additional interactions: confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls under the matched-budget constraints. These counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure, but assessing operational feasibility (the verifier tax tradeoffs) at NetOps scale requires larger deployments and throughput/latency benchmarking.

Failure modes, verifier-exploitation, and safety boundary. Per-episode validator traces show the principal residual failure modes in baseline were edits that (a) omit required restore steps (FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH), or (b) introduce or leave protected-interface edits (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE) and unintended modifications (UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE). Guarded repairs reduced these residuals on the controlled bank. Prior work warns that optimizing against a single verifier proxy can produce verifier-exploitation over longer iterative horizons; our short-horizon, single-repair opportunity design and paired shared-candidate semantics reduce but do not eliminate that risk [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10187492/v1]. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation (explicitly defined by PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE occurrences) was not computed in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory safety claims; the frozen mapping plus per-episode traces recorded enable deterministic recomputation by auditors.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: nondeterministic model sampling (temperature = null/unset) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair limit inference about generation determinism; differences isolate diagnostics exposure under the execution contract. Construct validity: primary success required agreement of a deterministic validator and a simulator; the simulator and validator together define the operational meaning of “valid” in this study. External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank; generalization to diverse vendor equipment, live operator streams, and different models/adapters is limited. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 provided sufficient power to detect the observed contrast but limits precision for per-fault-class or subgroup claims.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier and simulator used in execution. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered safety statistic. We recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications, explicit computation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation from archived traces, and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
